back: Energy from a source that is naturally replaced and will not run out on a human time scale: solar, wind, HEP, geothermal, tidal, wave, biomass.
Energy from a finite source used faster than it forms: coal, oil, natural gas and uranium.
Coal, oil and natural gas, formed over millions of years from buried plant and animal remains; burning them releases carbon dioxide.
Either: renewable if trees regrow or are replanted as fast as they are cut; non-renewable if woodland is cleared faster than it regrows.
Methane-rich gas made when dung and plant waste rot without air in a sealed digester; used for cooking and lighting, leaving fertiliser slurry.
Heat from hot rocks underground used to make steam for electricity, e.g. Olkaria in Kenya's Rift Valley.
Kariba South (HEP, Zambezi) and Hwange (coal-fired thermal).
Agriculture (tractors, irrigation, curing), mining (pumps, hoists, smelting), manufacturing (machines, furnaces); shortages raise costs and cut output.
Koeberg, near Cape Town in South Africa, is Africa's only nuclear power station.
